contract.review_scope: Complete captured body structure and stated guarded control values; opaque selector labels, callers and operational acceptance remain bounded gaps.
contract.purpose: Queue one DIF incoming message per qualifying container for a reprint flow.
inputs_defaults: INTERNAL nvarchar(max), username nvarchar(200), error nvarchar(2000) OUTPUT, success nvarchar(2000) OUTPUT; all required, no defaults. username/error/success are not used or assigned.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: NULL selector produces no cursor rows. Non-numeric selector can fail implicit comparison conversion. Duplicate container IDs are not deduplicated; Container IDs are concatenated without an escaping function; message-format validity is delegated to the downstream consumer.
output_shape: No result set; output error/success variables are left unchanged.

ordered_branches.explanation: Open FAST_FORWARD READ_ONLY cursor on shipping containers whose LAUNCH_NUM equals the supplied value, whose container ID is non-NULL and whose status is numeric 300.
Concatenate each container ID into a fixed message envelope and insert a DIF_INCOMING_MESSAGE row with Ready state, UTC stamps and fixed routing values.
Fetch until exhausted; close and deallocate the cursor on normal completion.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Only the explicitly described persistent writes occur in this body.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: Fixed routing/event/source values are opaque, not current endpoint evidence. Numeric status 300 has no verified business label in this contract.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH or error-output assignment; failure can stop midway without the normal cursor cleanup statements. SQL error propagation is not reflected in the named output variables.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transaction, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced. Caller/session transaction semantics govern effects.
concurrency: No deduplication key check or body-owned transaction across message inserts; reruns can queue repeated requests and failure can leave a partial batch.
contract.trigger_behavior: Persistent DML may activate configured table triggers; transitive trigger/caller behavior is separate from the direct body.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: DIF processing, actual rendering, delivery, retries and final printing are external. An inserted Ready message is a request, not proof of completion.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
